problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13997987/assets/671c38715438bb2a4b2ccf72a71765dadff1f2ed741ac52db7d4b70de43eee18.png)

Which of the following sets of parametric equations, defined for $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ),$ generate the parabola shown above?
worked_solution:
The diagram shows that the parabola is vertical, has its vertex at $(0,0),$ and passes through the point $(2,-4).$

The parametric equations of a vertical parabola  that has its vertex at $(0,0)$ are

$$
x=2pt,\,y=p{t}^{2},
$$

where $p$ is constant.

Since the parabola passes through $(2,-4),$ we can substitute $x=2$ and $y=-4$ into the standard parametric equations to obtain a system of equations. This gives

$$
{\begin{aligned}2=2pt \\ -4=p{t}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the first equation for $t,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}2 & =2pt \\ 1 & =pt \\ t & =\frac{1}{p}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting this into the second equation and solving for $p,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}-4 & =p{(\frac{1}{p})}^{2} \\ -4 & =p\cdot \frac{1}{{p}^{2}} \\ -4 & =\frac{1}{p} \\ p & =-\frac{1}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the parametric equations of the parabola are

$$
x=2(-\frac{1}{4})t,\,y=(-\frac{1}{4}){t}^{2},
$$

which simplify to

$$
x=-\frac{1}{2}t,\,y=-\frac{1}{4}{t}^{2}.
$$

Question 5

Which of the following sets of parametric equations, defined for t∈(−∞,∞), generate the parabola shown above?

a
x=t,y=t2
b
x=−t,y=t2
c
x=8t2,y=−8t
d
x=2t2,y=−4t
e
x=−12t,y=−14t2
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The diagram shows that the parabola is vertical, has its vertex at (0,0), and passes through the point (2,−4).

The parametric equations of a vertical parabola that has its vertex at (0,0) are

x=2pt,y=pt2,

where p is constant.

Since the parabola passes through (2,−4), we can substitute x=2 and y=−4 into the standard parametric equations to obtain a system of equations. This gives

{2=2pt−4=pt2.

Solving the first equation for t, we have

2=2pt1=ptt=1p.

Substituting this into the second equation and solving for p, we get

−4=p(1p)2−4=p⋅1p2−4=1pp=−14.

Therefore, the parametric equations of the parabola are

x=2(−14)t,y=(−14)t2,

which simplify to

x=−12t,y=−14t2.
